content.content:
=== vt-osc-0x9c-title-truncation.md

Found 2026-08-12: `charmbracelet/x/ansi`'s transition table (parser/transition_table.go)
extends OSC string data to bytes 0x20–0xFF for UTF-8, but still maps raw 0x9C
(8-bit ST) in OscStringState to DispatchAction. Any OSC 0/1/2 title containing a
UTF-8 rune with a 0x9C byte — Claude Code's spinner glyph `✳` (E2 9C B3), curly
quote `“` (E2 80 9C) — dispatches mid-rune: title becomes e.g. the lone byte
`\xe2` (renders as `�`), and the rest of the title text leaks onto the screen as
printed text.

Affects both emulators built on it: termpane in the TUI (pane titled edge shows
`─[ � ]`, window title gets the raw invalid byte) and the sandbox-agent shim's
screenBuffer (stores the mangled title and replays it on every attach). Verified
by probing live sandbox shims (several stored exactly `\xe2`) and by feeding the
sequences to `vt.Emulator` directly.

Proper fix is upstream (make string states UTF-8 aware, or drop the 0x9C
transition the way xterm does in UTF-8 mode); a local `replace` to a patched
fork works meanwhile. Related: [[vt-screen-buffer-deadlock]].
=== three-repo-split.md

As of 2026-08-22 the tree is three repositories: `discobox-ai/discobox`,
`discobox-ai/x` (generic libs: gormdb, gitutil, id, shorttmp, frontmatter — knows
nothing about Discobox), and `discobox-ai/hooks` (the `discobox-hooks` tool,
consumed by discobox as a Go tool dependency in the root `go.mod`).

**Why:** a change that spans the format or the shared libs is now three commits in
three repos, and the ordering matters — x first, then its consumers.

**How to apply:** after pushing to x or hooks, `go get <mod>@main` in discobox can
resolve to a *stale* pseudo-version because the module proxy caches `@main`; use
`GOPROXY=direct go get <mod>@main` when the bump silently no-ops. Every discobox
module must resolve x at one pseudo-version — bump `.`, `cli`, `server`,
`pool-agent`, `sandbox-agent` together, then `go tool task tidy`.

Anything that must be readable by both discobox and hooks belongs in x, not in the
discobox root module — hooks importing discobox would undo the split. See
[[adr-number-collisions-on-rebase]].
=== task-dev-breaks-rebase.md

`go tool task dev` runs `discobox-docker-image-watch` and `watchnbuild`, and the
`.discobox/hooks` regeneration hooks (`10-gofmt.sh`, `30-openapi-generate.sh`)
fire on every file change. During a `git rebase` each replayed commit looks like
a file change, so the watchers rewrite `api/gen/oas_*.go`, `api/openapi/server.yaml`
and gofmt-touched `.go` files *while the replay is in flight*. The rebase then
refuses to continue with a dirty tree, and `git rebase --abort` can itself be
blocked by files the watchers left untracked.

**Why:** observed 2026-09-11 rebasing 42 commits onto upstream/main. First attempt
wedged at commit 9/42 with 57 files dirty; second attempt, with `task dev` stopped,
replayed all 42 with only the expected content conflicts.

**How to apply:** before a rebase, check `pgrep -f 'task dev'` and stop it (ask the
user — it is their dev loop). Do **not** restart it afterwards unless asked: on
2026-09-23 I stopped two loops for a rebase, restarted one unprompted, and the
user's next words were "please stop it if so". Stopping it to unblock a rebase is
the job; deciding it should be running again is theirs. Leave it stopped and say
so. Stopping needs the process *group* (`kill -TERM -<pid>`) plus a `pkill` of
`watchnbuild|docker-image-watch|dev-lock` — a plain `kill` on the `task dev` pid
leaves every watcher alive.
Tag the pre-rebase tip first as a safety net. If an
abort is blocked by untracked files, compare them to the tip with `git cat-file -p`
before removing — they are usually byte-identical and safe to delete. Unrelated to
the Syncthing hazard in [[syncthing-git-corruption]], though both live on this
checkout. ADR collisions during the replay: [[adr-number-collisions-on-rebase]].
=== syncthing-git-corruption.md

`/home/darren/src` is a Syncthing folder (`lbtwo-l4kkp`) shared between
`beenie` (M3536N3, the WSL box) and `Station76` (TPGNN4T), so `.git` itself is
replicated. Several times a day `git status` fails with `fatal: bad object
HEAD`: `refs/heads/main` names a commit whose object has not arrived yet.

**CORRECTED 2026-09-10 — an earlier version of this memory was wrong.** It said
the objects were permanently lost and that waiting does not help. Both claims
were false, and acting on them created duplicate history twice.

**What is actually happening.** Ordering, not loss. Syncthing replicates files
independently (`order: random`); git requires objects to be durable before any
pointer to them. A ref is 41 bytes, a commit's objects are many files, so the
pointer wins the race. Measured windows: `d084ad18` broke git at 17:41 and was
delivered 17:47:16 (~6 min); `d6a0354c` broke it at ~18:24, delivered 19:00:03
(~35 min). Verified via `/rest/db/file` — the objects carry `version=
['TPGNN4T:…']`, i.e. Syncthing delivered them from the other device.

**So: WAIT. Do not hand-repair.** Hand-repair builds a second history for work
that is about to arrive; the original commits then sit dangling beside the
replacements. That happened on 2026-09-09 with both incidents.

**The index is never corrupted.** All 56 `.git/index.sync-conflict-*` copies in
the folder validate byte-perfect (DIRC magic + correct trailing SHA-1). The
index is mutable and not content-addressed so it genuinely conflicts and
recency picks a winner — a *valid* index belonging to the other machine's
state. `invalid sha1 pointer in cache-tree of .git/index` names the index but
means the tree object it references has not landed. Objects themselves never
conflict (content-addressed); they are only present or absent.

**Root cause (verified 2026-09-10 over ssh):** Station76 (`ssh
192.168.1.185`; the name does not resolve) runs Syncthing v1.30.0, up since
2026-08-18, and its watcher holds inotify watches on only 2 of 256
`.git/objects/xx` dirs (and not `logs/`) — watches lost over time on dirs that
predate its start. So its new objects are announced only at the hourly full
rescan while refs (watched) go out in ~10 s. A probe object went unindexed for
40 s; `POST /rest/db/scan?sub=disco2/.git` indexed it in 0.4 s. beenie (v2.1.3)
watches all 257. Likely cause: Station76 has NESTED folders — `home`
(`dt67u-ny6fq`, /home/darren, 1.39M files, shared with odroid I6KJIOQ) around
`src`, `bin`, `bashrc` — unsupported by Syncthing; `.git/logs` is unwatched
=== hooks-force-rerun.md

`go tool task check-hooks` queries a background hooks daemon; the daemon runs hooks against the **live working tree** (not a snapshot/worktree). Stale/failed results appear when the daemon hasn't re-run since recent edits.

**Why:** A failing check-hooks result can be a stale daemon run, not a real failure — don't trust it blindly, and don't blame Docker build cache first.

**How to apply:** Force a specific hook to re-run with `cd hooks && go run ./cmd/discobox-hooks run <HOOK_ID> --force` (e.g. `dockerfile-test-builds`), then inspect `... runs <HOOK_ID>` for the newest result. See the `run` subcommand in [[hooks-cli]].
=== exec-terminal-consolidation.md

DONE (2026-07-08, branch `consolidate-exec-terminal`): collapsed the two
parallel sandbox runtime constructs — `sandbox-agent/execs` and
`sandbox-agent/terminal` — into ONE primitive (`exec`). A "terminal" is now an
exec created in agent mode, built as a layer on top. All phases A–E landed;
repo builds, `test:all` and `check-hooks` green.

**Why:** the two managers/shims/systemd-runners are ~80% identical; agent
resolution, installer, and primary/resume are pre-command orchestration, so
`execs.Manager` can stay an agnostic process/PTY runner and `terminal` becomes a
pure consumer of it. Attach mechanics are already shared via `shimruntime`.

**How to apply:**
- `execs.Manager` stays agent-agnostic. Add: optional caller-supplied
  `CreateRequest.ID`, `Delete`+`Stop` (lift from terminal/systemd.go),
  metadata-based filtering. Terminal-ness lives only in command + metadata
  (`agentId`, `primary`).
- Reimplement `terminal` as `terminal.Service` over `execs.Manager` (agent
  resolve, `Installer` family, `EnsurePrimary`/resume, default user). Delete
  terminal's parallel Manager/systemd/shim (~2100 lines → ~500).
- `resources.Collector`/`store` retarget at execs; rename store `TerminalID`
  → `ExecID`; resource collection becomes opt-in per exec.
- Unify attach on the exec WebSocket path; retire terminal HTTP-Upgrade.
  Ctrl-P Q detach stays a client-side CLI concern.
- API surface DECISION: collapse to `/execs` only. `create` takes `command` OR
  `agentId`+`args`. `/agent-terminals/*` removed. `terminal` survives as a CLI
  verb + create mode. UI must migrate off agent-terminals (phase 6).
- Phasing: 1) merge systemd runners/shims/helpers 2) exec Delete/Stop + caller
  ID 3) terminal.Service over execs.Manager 4) retarget resources/events
  5) unify attach 6) API/CLI collapse + UI migration.

Relates to [[agent-config-layered-definitions]].
=== kody-github-digest-job.md

Darren's Kody account (kody.codes, user `ibuildthecloud`, inbox
`ibuildthecloud@inbox.heykody.dev`) runs an hourly GitHub notification digest
job, id `bc93f97a-25c6-4ff0-9598-efc6f1b93e75`, cron `0 * * * *` America/Denver.
Local snapshot of its source: `~/kody-gh-digest.job.ts`.

Non-obvious facts learned the hard way:

- The GitHub OAuth integration is named **`github-platform`**, not `github`.
  The official `provider_github` guide's Lane A URL
  (`/connect/oauth?provider=github`) fails with "Missing required OAuth
  configuration parameters" — use the slug from `integration_platform_app_list`.
- `repo` scope covers `GET /notifications`; the `notifications` scope is not
  required. Org OAuth App restrictions do not filter notifications from
  **public** repos, so obot-platform's unapprovable "Request" does not matter.
- Durable KV inside a job is the ambient `storage` object from `kody:runtime`
  (`await storage.get/set`). `packageStorage()` throws outside a package, and
  `kody.storage()` proxies to a nonexistent tool ("Tool \"storage\" not found").
  `storage` is only bound inside a job, never in ad-hoc `execute`.
- `job_get({ includeCode: true })` returns source at **`source.code`**, not
  `job.code`; the response is `{ job, alarm, source }`.
- `email_send` only accepts your own account email as recipient (goes to
  darren@obot.ai). Free plan: 10 sends/day.
- Jobs have no per-job permission scoping — they run with full ambient account
  authority. Narrowing lives on the secret (`allowed_hosts`,
  `allowed_capabilities`, `allowed_packages`) and is settable only from
  `/account/secrets`, not by an agent. `allowed_packages` can only name
  packages, so scoping that way excludes standalone jobs.

=== vt-osc-0x9c-title-truncation.md

Found 2026-08-12: `charmbracelet/x/ansi`'s transition table (parser/transition_table.go)
extends OSC string data to bytes 0x20–0xFF for UTF-8, but still maps raw 0x9C
(8-bit ST) in OscStringState to DispatchAction. Any OSC 0/1/2 title containing a
UTF-8 rune with a 0x9C byte — Claude Code's spinner glyph `✳` (E2 9C B3), curly
quote `“` (E2 80 9C) — dispatches mid-rune: title becomes e.g. the lone byte
`\xe2` (renders as `�`), and the rest of the title text leaks onto the screen as
printed text.

Affects both emulators built on it: termpane in the TUI (pane titled edge shows
`─[ � ]`, window title gets the raw invalid byte) and the sandbox-agent shim's
screenBuffer (stores the mangled title and replays it on every attach). Verified
by probing live sandbox shims (several stored exactly `\xe2`) and by feeding the
sequences to `vt.Emulator` directly.

Proper fix is upstream (make string states UTF-8 aware, or drop the 0x9C
transition the way xterm does in UTF-8 mode); a local `replace` to a patched
fork works meanwhile. Related: [[vt-screen-buffer-deadlock]].

As of 2026-08-22 the tree is three repositories: `discobox-ai/discobox`,
`discobox-ai/x` (generic libs: gormdb, gitutil, id, shorttmp, frontmatter — knows
nothing about Discobox), and `discobox-ai/hooks` (the `discobox-hooks` tool,

=== task-dev-breaks-rebase.md

`go tool task dev` runs `discobox-docker-image-watch` and `watchnbuild`, and the
`.discobox/hooks` regeneration hooks (`10-gofmt.sh`, `30-openapi-generate.sh`)
fire on every file change. During a `git rebase` each replayed commit looks like
a file change, so the watchers rewrite `api/gen/oas_*.go`, `api/openapi/server.yaml`
and gofmt-touched `.go` files *while the replay is in flight*. The rebase then
refuses to continue with a dirty tree, and `git rebase --abort` can itself be
blocked by files the watchers left untracked.

**Why:** observed 2026-09-11 rebasing 42 commits onto upstream/main. First attempt
wedged at commit 9/42 with 57 files dirty; second attempt, with `task dev` stopped,
replayed all 42 with only the expected content conflicts.

user — it is their dev loop). Do **not** restart it afterwards unless asked: on

user's next words were "please stop it if so". Stopping it to unblock a rebase is
the job; deciding it should be running again is theirs. Leave it stopped and say

content.text:
No, nothing else in memory needs a code fix. The cleanup bug you just filed as #314 was the only open product bug in my notes. One other note described a bug, and it turned out to be fixed already.

**Already fixed: the window-title bug.** A note from 2026-08-12 said the terminal parser garbled any title containing `✳` or curly quotes (`“ ”`), which Claude Code's titles use. The title came out as `�`, and the rest of it spilled onto the screen. Every module now swaps in your fork `discobox-ai/charm-x` for that parser. I ran a quick throwaway test with `✳ Claude “x”` and it came through intact. The original library still has the bug, so sending the fix upstream would let you drop the fork. I've marked the note fixed.

**Not product bugs:**
- **Syncthing and `.git`.** On this machine and Station76, git refs can arrive before the objects they point to, which breaks `git status` for minutes at a time. The note blames Station76's Syncthing: it misses changes in most `.git/objects` folders, likely because of its nested shared folders. That's a fix to how the two machines are set up, not to discobox, and nothing says it's been done.
- **Working tips.** The rest are habits rather than defects:
  - Stop `task dev` before rebasing.
  - Use `GOPROXY=direct` when bumping the `x` or `hooks` modules.
  - Force a re-run when a `check-hooks` result is stale.
  - Watch for ADR number collisions on rebase.

The rest are history or design notes, such as the terminal deadlock fixed in July and finished refactors.
